title: What happened in AI — Nov 10, 2026
intro: Agent safety moved to enforcement points: tools that intercept commands, audit access and test database roles shipped alongside NVIDIA donating OpenShell to the CNCF.
Google made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available and DeepMind formally verified Signal's protocol code with agents, while the Fireworks AI breach spread to customer data.
highlights: Gemini 4 Carbon is generally available, with a new multimodal agent benchmark (MKA) alongside it.
DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verified security properties of Signal's real protocol code.
NVIDIA is donating its OpenShell agent-governance runtime to the CNCF.
A read-only Postgres role does not stop every harmful agent query; a reproducible test shows which ones.
Fireworks AI's breach now includes billing data and some customer secrets; Notion is notifying users.
Epoch: GB300 has 25x H100's agentic inference capacity on only 2.5x the FLOP/s.

categories.name: Guardrails on What Agents Can Touch
categories.summary: Builders are moving agent safety from prompts to enforcement points: database roles, command interceptors, access audits and a CNCF-bound agent runtime.

articles.title: What a read-only Postgres role does and doesn't stop when an AI agent connects
articles.summary: A reproducible PostgreSQL 17.11 run shows which harms a read-only role blocks and which session settings and reads still get through.

articles.title: Antelog – stops AI coding agents from running dangerous commands
articles.summary: Local interceptor that checks each shell command a coding agent proposes and pauses destructive ones, like deleting a production volume, for approval.

articles.title: I Access Auditor – see and revoke what your AI coding agents can access
articles.summary: Desktop app that inventories what Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and OpenCode can access, and lets you revoke it.

articles.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
articles.summary: NVIDIA is donating OpenShell, its runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the CNCF as a Sandbox project.

articles.title: Show HN: Fix Gate – verifies security-fix PRs, incl. AI-written ones
articles.summary: Rule-based GitHub Action that checks a security-fix PR: finding gone, nothing new, files parse, tests not newly failed; unrun checks never count as passes.

categories.name: Agent Experience: Docs and APIs Now Have an Agent Audience
categories.summary: Agent traffic to docs is now large enough to measure, and vendors are starting to design SDKs and docs for the agent that picks them.

articles.title: Measure agent-traffic for any site
articles.summary: Open-source tool from Mintlify to measure how much of a site's traffic is agents, which ones, and whether a GPTBot request is really OpenAI.

articles.title: What Is Agent Experience (Ax)?
articles.summary: Microsoft defines AX: an agent picking a rival service or calling a deprecated API makes your product look broken, so measure it.

articles.title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
articles.summary: Resend's Zeno Rocha on where answer-engine optimization ends and agent experience begins, from docs Claude Code reads to tools it calls.

articles.title: Show HN: Get your coding agent off ~2019 JavaScript, onto modern web primitives
articles.summary: Agent skill that steers coding agents off legacy JavaScript patterns toward native browser primitives like CSS.highlights and dialog.

categories.name: Verifying and Operating Agent-Built Software
categories.summary: The verification bar for agent output is rising, from formal proofs of real protocol code to evidence that messy codebases derail coding agents.

articles.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
articles.summary: DeepMind's agentic framework formally verified key security properties of the actual Signal protocol code.

articles.title: Google Finds that Technical Debt Can Derail Coding Agents Through "Agent Distraction"
articles.summary: Google research finds technical debt causes "agent distraction" that throws coding agents off task.

articles.title: Article: LLM Reliability Layers Under Test: Accuracy, Yield, and the Limits of Verification
articles.summary: InfoQ tests LLM reliability layers on accuracy and yield, and maps where verification stops helping.

articles.title: How Workday Built an Enterprise-Scale AI Agent Platform with LangGraph and LangSmith
articles.summary: Workday's internal agent platform uses LangGraph for orchestration and LangSmith for tracing and evals, targeting production agents by end of 2026.

categories.name: Frontier and Small Model Releases
categories.summary: Three labs shipped on the same news cycle: Google's top tier, Anthropic's Fable 5.2, and Meta's smallest Muse model.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
articles.summary: Google's strongest model is now generally available, pitched on cybersecurity and long-horizon agentic work, after a two-week defender-only preview.

articles.title: The Multimodal Knowledge Agent Benchmark
articles.summary: New Google and Artificial Analysis benchmark for agents that must reason over visually complex files, not just text.

articles.title: [AINews] Fable 5.2 retakes World #1 LLM spot as $ANT IPO roadshow begins
articles.summary: Latent Space covers Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 retaking the top LLM spot as Anthropic's IPO roadshow opened.

articles.title: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember
articles.summary: Meta's small, efficient model enters the Haiku/Luna tier, per Simon Willison's notes.

articles.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro Coder Arrives at 775 GB, Built to Fit One GPU
articles.summary: Moonshot's coding model ships as a 775 GB release aimed at fitting on a single GPU.

categories.name: Inference Economics: Memory, State and Mixed Hardware
categories.summary: Inference gains now come from memory, state reuse and plumbing more than raw FLOP/s.

articles.title: Beyond FLOP/s: comparing AI hardware for inference by memory and communication
articles.summary: Epoch estimates GB300 delivers about 25x H100's agentic inference capacity per chip with only 2.5x the 8-bit FLOP/s.

articles.title: FlashStates Unlocking Flexible Hybrid State Management for Agentic LLM Inference
articles.summary: Together AI and collaborators decouple recurrent checkpoints from KV-cache blocks so hybrid models can resume agent sessions without dense state storage.

articles.title: CUDA+ROCm dual-back ends LLM inference for mixed-vendor GPUs (up to 48% faster)
articles.summary: Patch splits GLM MoE inference across an RTX 5090 and a Radeon iGPU, CUDA for attention and HIP for experts, reporting up to 48% faster.

articles.title: Show HN: QueenMQ – slow LLM calls blocked our Kafka partitions, so we built it
articles.summary: Apache-2.0 message broker built after slow LLM calls blocked Kafka partitions; it has mostly replaced Kafka at its authors' company.

categories.name: Inference Vendor Breach Widens
categories.summary: The Fireworks AI incident now reaches customer data, and downstream apps are notifying their own users.

articles.title: Fireworks.ai Update on October 2026 security incident
articles.summary: Fireworks now reports impact to account and billing data and, for some accounts, secrets, datasets and incomplete models.

articles.title: Tell HN: Notion AI chat sessions have been exposed via Fireworks AI hack
articles.summary: Notion is emailing users that AI chat sessions may be exposed through its vendor Fireworks AI.
